- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict high outcomes — adjust forecast upward, especially in early/medium horizon.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33) and price is trending up, model often overreacts with sharp spikes — cap or dampen forecast peaks, especially in short-term (1-7 days).
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike (e.g., 3-5 day high followed by drop), model often overcorrects — reduce forecast magnitude in subsequent days.
- Model frequently underestimates long-term (15-30 day) outcomes when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — increase baseline forecast for horizon >15 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model often lags — anticipate early rebound and adjust forecast upward 1-3 days ahead.
- If model forecast shows “overshoot” (e.g., 3-5 day peak > true outcome), reduce forecast by 15-30% in next 3-5 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- For sentiment history with repeated 0.00 values, model tends to be overly conservative — increase forecast by 10-20% for horizon >10 days.
